output.summary: A deciduous shrub native to nearly all of Europe, northern and central Asia, Japan, Greenland, western Canada and the western United States. It spreads by rhizomes into broad patches, and its light-green leaves redden before falling. Its edible blue-black berries contain pigment in both skin and flesh and are widely used in cooking.
output.edibilityNote: The berries are edible and commonly used in pies, cakes, jams, sauces, syrups, juices and sweets; the leaves may be unsafe to consume.
